Folks —

Following Ellen's reply I sketched an execution checklist so we can move quickly:

1) Legal redline approval (Rishi) — confirm language for UK Supplement and our standard subprocessor notice window (target: same day).
2) TIA response — Neha to prepare a 1-page Q&A addressing Acme_TIA_questions.pdf.
3) Finalize DPA PDF with accepted redlines and upload to DocuSign. Include field for PO number and a signature block for Acme's authorized signer.
4) DocuSign envelope sent and tracked in HubSpot (I'll update the deal stage to "contracting" once sent).
5) Post-signature: automated subprocessor notification schedule (30-day window) and an internal alert to Solutions Engineering to hold any onboarding that would process Acme data until the notice window passes.

If any of the steps need alternative routing (AdobeSign, longer notice window), flag now. I recommend we keep the 30 days — it balances agility and Acme's security needs.

Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 3 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + subprocessors list (first pass)

Marissa / team —

I've reviewed the redlines and Acme's TIA questions. High-level guidance and suggested language below. Happy to jump on a call to walk through.

1) Transfers: we can accept execution of the EU SCCs (2021) and provide a short UK Supplement that: (a) confirms applicability of UK data transfer rules, (b) maps the SCC roles/obligations back to the DPA, and (c) includes a targeted paragraph about transfers to US-hosted subprocessors (controls + engineering safeguards). Suggested phrasing: "To the extent Personal Data is transferred to processors or subprocessors located outside the UK, Controller and Processor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures consistent with the SCCs and as described in Redwood's Transfer Impact Assessment summary."

2) Subprocessors: 30-day advance notice is acceptable. Add an explicit escalation path: Acme may object in writing within 15 days of notice; parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate; if unresolved, either party may suspend processing of Acme data for the impacted workload pending alternative arrangements.

3) TIA responses: Neha, please include: (i) hosting locations (region-level), (ii) encryption in transit/at rest, (iii) access control model, (iv) subprocessors list + primary function, (v) logging/audit capabilities. Keep it to one page, bulleted.

4) Execution: DocuSign preferred. When creating the envelope, include a "PO number" custom field and a checkbox for "UK Supplement included" so procurement can sign off.

If Acme requires additional contractual assurances (e.g., DPA exhibits listing specific technical measures), we can attach a short technical annex rather than re-opening the DPA.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
